drone-pilot-pathway.summary: NSW national parks: commercial drone filming needs prior NPWS approval on top of CASA rules.

items.text: Commercial drone filming or photography in NSW national parks and reserves needs prior NPWS approval (not available under a small-scale filming permit). Apply at least 10 business days ahead with CASA compliance, flight plan, risk assessment, licences and insurance.
2026-27 fees include a drone fee on top of the filming application fee (NPWS fee schedule).

laws.rule: NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service requires approval to launch, land or operate a drone in its national parks and reserves. For personal recreation apply to the relevant park office at least 10 days beforehand; some parks do not allow recreational use. Commercial filming follows a separate application.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: NSW National Parks says campfires may not be permitted in all parks, and visitors should use designated fireplaces and obey park and total fire bans. Do not collect fallen timber or break branches; check whether to bring firewood.

laws.rule: NSW National Parks says domestic animals are not permitted in most NSW national parks; check the individual park and permitted-animal provisions before taking a pet.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: When visiting Aboriginal cultural sites in NSW national parks, avoid hand or foot contact with the site; leave rocks, artefacts and vegetation as you find them; do not re-groove, chalk or draw on the site; and do not place water or sand on it. Sites can be fragile because of weathering and erosion.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Aboriginal cultural sites in parks include rock art and stone artefacts. The page does not list a statewide photography ban or closed-site list; follow any site-specific signs.
